standard_prerequisites.name: Fraisse structures, their ages, and the quotients of the automorphism group
standard_prerequisites.statement: The paper works with a Fraisse structure based on the natural numbers, its age, that is the class of its finite substructures, and its automorphism group; the finite sets of embeddings of a finite substructure into the structure are written as binomial symbols, and the quotient of the automorphism group by the stabiliser of a finite substructure is identified with the set of embeddings of that substructure, whose image under an automorphism is again such a set. A colouring of such a set of embeddings is a map into a finite set of colours, and being constant up to a positive number on a set of embeddings means that its values on that set vary by at most that number. The author's own notation is retained inside the counted statement and proof.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted proposition is the combinatorial criterion that the paper uses to pass between statements about finite colorings and statements about the orbits of the automorphism group, and it is invoked by the Ramsey-type results of the same section.

core_obligations: Translate finite subsets of the group into finite sets of embeddings: for a finite substructure and a finite set of automorphisms, the classes of those automorphisms in the quotient by the stabiliser can be identified with the restrictions of their inverses, hence with a finite set of embeddings, which is contained in the set of embeddings of the given substructure into some larger finite substructure (source lines 328-332).

Compute the translate of such a set: the set of classes of the translates of the automorphisms by a fixed element coincides with the set of restrictions of the translated inverses, which is the set of embeddings into the image of the larger substructure under that element, giving the displayed inclusion (source lines 332-334).

Prove the converse translation: for a finite substructure there is a finite set of automorphisms whose classes contain every embedding of the given substructure into it, and translating that set by an element produces a set containing the embeddings into the image of the substructure (source lines 336-337).

Conclude the equivalence: starting from either of the two statements, one substitutes the translated description of the finite sets of embeddings to obtain the other, and the last two paragraphs of the proof carry out the two directions (source lines 337-338).

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the classes of finitely many automorphisms with a finite set of embeddings and embed it into a set of embeddings of a larger finite substructure.
Compute the translate of that set as the set of embeddings into the image of the larger substructure.
Show the converse translation from a finite substructure to a finite set of automorphisms.
Carry out the two directions of the equivalence and conclude.

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Proposition prop:aOSRamsey at source lines 318-325 together with its proof at source lines 327-338, a straight adjacent pairing in the source file. The source is the publisher version of the article in Annales Henri Lebesgue 2 (2019), pages 149-185, DOI 10.5802/ahl.16, released under CC BY 4.0.

The licence evidence for this card is the inherited publisher-version record kept with the source: LICENSE_EVIDENCE.json names the publisher version, the licence CC BY 4.0 and its URL, quotes the notice on the closing page of the publisher PDF, and records the SHA-256 of that PDF, while inherited-license.txt restates author, work, version, DOI and licence. The source's own licence-observation.json records that the landing page displays no licence line and that the reuse basis is the inherited evidence; this lane verified the first article of the family and found no contradiction with the journal-level CC BY 4.0 statement, which is the check the Lead required for the AHL family. No acceptance record is written anywhere.

The retained preamble is the source's editorial preamble with three omissions only: the class line, which the assembler supplies; the page geometry; and the fontspec block with its explicit font files, which would fight the forced xelatex engine. The theorem declarations under the shared counter and the whole macro block are kept verbatim, so that the macros of the retained spans, including the boldface structure letter, the age symbol, the stabiliser and the restriction notation, are all available.

Neither the retained statement nor the retained proof contains a citation or a reference to another labelled result of the article, so this card carries no bibliography entry and no navigation pointer.

The statements in the census package were used as a starting point only: the statement span, the proof span and the absence of citations were re-read from the source before the card was written, as the census itself asks.
